key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks discover nonlinear water-wave candidates with near-machine-precision equation residuals, with one candidate independently certified using interval arithmetic and Lean.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers an auditable route to highly accurate nonlinear free-surface wave computations for computational fluid mechanics.
method: Learn wave profiles, speeds and continuation surface tension directly from governing equations without training data.
Use staged training and refinement to recover Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples and explore new candidates.
Freeze one candidate, certify its uniform residual bound with interval arithmetic and machine-check the certification deductions in Lean.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-machine-precision residuals in strongly nonlinear regimes and rigorous certification of one candidate accounting for roundoff, Fourier truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors.
watch_item: A certified small residual does not by itself establish existence or uniqueness of a nearby exact solution, and the reported certification covers one candidate.
paper_title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
